description: Save what this task has established. Each collection is independent: an item that fails does not discard the others, and each one is reported separately. Omission preserves what is already saved. Saving does not finish the task. Collections are optional arrays. Each write must carry at least one item in a nonempty collection or a non-null scalar value; controls alone save nothing. A rejected item blocks COMPLETE delivery: resend it under its collection; an accepted version of the same item supersedes the rejected proposal, not a proof that its old scientific claim was corrected. Use a different item identity for an additional fact. Choose disposition PARTIAL to stop with unresolved writes; the host records them in the delivery without marking them repaired.

conflicts.description: Choose which reading is primary when a finding contradicts the skeleton. Identity: finding. An item sent again with the same finding replaces the saved one; to change the finding of a saved item, quote its item_id. No other id is needed. primary: SKELETON, FINDING.

anyOf.description: Explicitly adopt the linked finding's current explanation as this ruling's reason.

from_finding.description: Use the linked finding's current explanation as this ruling's reason.

explanation.description: Why this experimental reading takes priority or the skeleton is retained. Apply the shared route conventions to the evidence and scope at this position.

finding.description: finding_id of the conflicting reading being adjudicated.

item_id.description: Host-issued handle returned when this item was first saved; quote it only to change the fields that identify the item (its collection says which), and omit it for a new item.

primary.description: SKELETON retains the route reading as primary; FINDING chooses the cited finding as primary, with evidence explained.

findings.description: Identity: finding_id (your own name for it). An item sent again with the same finding_id replaces the saved one; to change the finding_id of a saved item, quote its item_id. No other id is needed. aspect: condition, material, yield, characterization, name, assertion, new_compound, elision, nothing_to_record, intermediate, measurement_products. relation: SAME, ADDS, CONTRADICTS. value_relation: VALUE, ORDERED_POINTS. reporting_level: TOTAL, USE. scope: WHOLE, SEGMENT, PART, ANOTHER_EXPERIMENT, UNRESOLVED.

anyOf.description:
Common fields:
item_id: Host-issued handle returned when this item was first saved; quote it only to change the fields that identify the item (its collection says which), and omit it for a new item.
finding_id: Your name for this value; rulings name it in finding.
aspect: Select the declared kind of this one finding; its words must use that kind's declared shape. Do not write public field names or patch actions.
words: One author value, copied from cited evidence, using the text or structured word fields declared for the selected aspect.
category_word: What kind of condition it is. Prefer one of these keys, written as such: TEMPERATURE: a temperature the reaction is held at or brought to (reflux, -78 °C, rt); several on one operation are its profile in the order written; DURATION: how long the operation or a stage of it runs (2 h, overnight); ATMOSPHERE: the gas the reaction is run under (argon, N2, air, H2 balloon); PRESSURE: the pressure the reaction is run at (4 atm H2, 50 bar); the vacuum of a concentration or distillation is REDUCED_PRESSURE, not this; CONCENTRATION: the concentration of the reaction mixture (0.1 M, c = 0.05 M); the strength of a reagent's solution (2.5 M in hexanes, 1 M in THF) is part of that material's amount phrase, not a condition of its own; SCALE: the amount the operation is run on; on a MATERIAL, how much of it the author used: his whole phrase for the amount, copied as written with every quantity and qualifier in it (26 mg (0.25 mmol, 1 equiv), 1.1 mL (0.55 mmol, 0.5 M in THF), 10 mol %, ten drops); the host reads the amount and the equivalents from it; ADDITION: how or in what order a material is added (dropwise, portionwise, over 30 min, added last); WORKUP: how the reaction is quenched, washed or extracted; purification does not by itself create a separate operation. Its media are QUENCH_WORKUP materials; MICROWAVE: heated by microwave irradiation (MW, μW); PHOTOCHEMICAL: driven by light: a lamp, LED or hv at a wavelength; keeping light out is LIGHT_EXCLUSION; SONICATION: run under ultrasound (sonication, ultrasonic bath); FLOW: run in continuous flow or a flow reactor rather than a flask; SEALED_VESSEL: run in a sealed tube, pressure tube, autoclave or bomb; an ordinary flask is not a condition; DEGASSED: the mixture or solvent was degassed (freeze-pump-thaw, sparged with an inert gas); bubbling a reactive gas through is that gas's ATMOSPHERE; ONE_POT: carried out in the same pot as the preceding operation without isolation (one-pot, telescoped, tandem); STOCK_SOLUTION: how a reagent solution was supplied or handled for use (titrated before use); the strength of a reagent's solution (2.5 M in hexanes, 1 M in THF) is part of that material's amount phrase, not a condition of its own. A separately prepared reagent is one material of the main operation. Its preparation ingredients and preparation conditions belong to another experiment: retain that procedure with its source and explanation, without adding its ingredients or conditions to the main operation. In an experimental reading, ANOTHER_EXPERIMENT keeps the reading separate. Preserve the complete account through the declared narrative entry; if the active declaration offers EXPERIMENT and its operations through skeleton_repairs, use those for an independent experimental graph. A narrative alone does not create that graph.; MONITORING: how completion was judged (monitored by TLC, until consumption of the starting material); STIRRING: a stated stirring or agitation regime (vigorous stirring, rpm); REDUCED_PRESSURE: under vacuum for a concentration, distillation or removal of a volatile (in vacuo, rotary evaporation, reduced pressure); LIGHT_EXCLUSION: kept from light (amber flask, wrapped in foil, in the dark); SOLVENT_RATIO: the proportion of mixed reaction solvents (THF:H2O 4:1, 8:1 THF/1 M NaOH); the solvents themselves are MATERIALs. Chromatography eluents and their ratios belong to QUENCH_WORKUP materials. If none fits, write your own word here and the host keeps the condition with a null key; text is always the author's own words.
condition_about: The material the condition is about, when it is about one; omitted otherwise.
selection_ids: Additional sources supporting ownership or continuous text; source selectors supply their own citations automatically. Use a supplied source selection permitted by this task's citation policy: delivered source content or a verified inherited source accompanying its meaning. A search hit or a source requested in this response is not yet citable.
value_selection_ids: Optional narrower source selections containing the exact value words; otherwise selection_ids provide the quotation evidence. Use a supplied source selection permitted by this task's citation policy: delivered source content or a verified inherited source accompanying its meaning. A search hit or a source requested in this response is not yet citable.
relation: Relation of scientific VALUES to the skeleton, not chemical identity. For a named existing position, SAME retains primary values without applying supplied additions to primary fields; complete source wording remains in the saved reading. ADDS (default) applies additional information, including a newly supplied amount for an existing material. CONTRADICTS records a conflicting reading for an explicit ruling. Material identity is expressed separately in words.identity_relation; the same chemical can have relation=ADDS.
value_relation: For a condition, VALUE is one value or interval. ORDERED_POINTS means the quoted endpoints are successive values in the author's order, including a shared unit. Decide from the whole procedure; the host will not infer this relation from words such as to or then.
sequence: Explicitly ordered condition members, any number. Each uses text or source_parts. When every member supplies its source, parent words may be omitted: the host retains their separate source fragments, without joining them.
shared_unit_text: Optional author-stated unit shared by sequence members; it must occur in the verified parent or member sources.
reporting_level: Material only: author-reported total or one use; omit if unspecified.
detail_of: Material only: this use is a detail of the named material finding or existing material. The summary may be written later in the same batch.
clear_summary: Material only: explicitly detach the selected existing use from its summary; retain the material and amount. Mutually exclusive with detail_of.
review_reason: Optional scientific uncertainty to review; it does not block supported facts.
scope: For materials, omitted scope retains the existing scope; explicit WHOLE clears a stage. WHOLE applies to the entire operation; SEGMENT names a declared stretch; PART is a stretch that cannot be distinguished; ANOTHER_EXPERIMENT describes another run or scale and has no segment_key. See the aspect's publication entry for supported public scopes and explicit experiment ownership. A separately prepared reagent is one material of the main operation. Its preparation ingredients and preparation conditions belong to another experiment: retain that procedure with its source and explanation, without adding its ingredients or conditions to the main operation. In an experimental reading, ANOTHER_EXPERIMENT keeps the reading separate. Preserve the complete account through the declared narrative entry; if the active declaration offers EXPERIMENT and its operations through skeleton_repairs, use those for an independent experimental graph. A narrative alone does not create that graph. For a new condition, omitted scope means UNRESOLVED, never WHOLE. When updating the same saved condition, omission retains its scope and stage. State a scope explicitly to change it; null is not a scope-clearing operation.
segment_key: Declared segment_key for scope SEGMENT, belonging to an operation in about_ids; otherwise null.
existing_stage_id: For a supported SEGMENT finding, select an existing stage shown on this operation instead of declaring it again. Mutually exclusive with segment_key.
skeleton_material_id: Exact host-issued material position id this material corresponds to, when any. The host retains skeleton materials not named by a finding.
block_id: Existing reaction-block id identifying the route step for this yield when needed; null if not established.
explanation: Explain the value's object, procedural scope and relation using its cited paragraph context.

role.description: The role this material serves in its operation. Choose one of these roles by its meaning: ROUTE_SUBSTRATE: the route compound the operation starts from and transforms, however the author names or numbers it; REAGENT: a substance added to bring the transformation about and consumed by it (a base, an oxidant, a reductant, an organometallic, an acid); CATALYST: a substance that brings the transformation about without being consumed by it (a metal complex, an organocatalyst, an acid or base used catalytically); ADDITIVE: a substance added to the reaction that is neither its reagent, its catalyst nor its solvent (a ligand, a salt, molecular sieves, an initiator, a stabilizer); SOLVENT: the medium the reaction itself runs in; a solvent used only to quench, extract, wash or purify is QUENCH_WORKUP; QUENCH_WORKUP: anything used after the reaction to stop it or to isolate or purify its product: a quench, a wash, an extraction solvent, a drying agent, a chromatography eluent (its ratio kept in its name), silica or celite.

kind.description: What kind of value the author reports. Choose one of these kinds by its meaning: ISOLATED_YIELD: the yield of a product the author isolated, with or without its mass (2.65 g (97%), 42 mg (52%), 70% isolated yield); REPORTED_YIELD: a yield the author states without saying how it was determined, as a scheme or the narrative often does (81% over 3 steps, quantitative); ASSAY_YIELD: a yield measured on the unpurified mixture by GC, HPLC or another calibrated assay; NMR_YIELD: a yield measured on the unpurified mixture by NMR against an internal standard; BRSM_YIELD: a yield based on recovered starting material (71% brsm); EE: the product's enantiomeric excess (98% ee); DR: the product's diastereomeric ratio, a single diastereomer included (3:1 dr, >20:1 d.r., single diastereomer); RATIO: any other ratio between products or isomers (E/Z 5:1, a regioisomer ratio, an enantiomeric ratio); RECOVERED_STARTING_MATERIAL: how much starting material was recovered unreacted (15% rsm, 323 mg (37%) of the starting diastereomer); SCALE: how much product a run made where the author states an amount but no yield (1.52 g of 14b); the amount a run is carried out on is the SCALE condition, not this.

An item sent again with the same title and kind replaces the saved one; to change the title or kind of a saved item, quote its item_id. No other id is needed. kind: OBJECTIVE, AUTHOR_CONCLUSION, ROUTE_STRATEGY, SCOPE, MECHANISM, STRUCTURAL_CONTEXT, RELATED_FIGURE, OPTIMIZATION, FAILED_ATTEMPT, BIOLOGICAL_FINDING.

author_selection_ids.description: Exact TEXT selections to retain as author quotations, copied byte for byte; empty for pure images.

explanation.description: Your source-grounded synthesis of the topic.

item_id.description: Host-issued handle returned when this item was first saved; quote it only to change the fields that identify the item (its collection says which), and omit it for a new item.

kind.description: The narrative's kind. BIOLOGICAL_FINDING is recorded in this channel's own receipt and never enters the main result.

selection_ids.description: Selection IDs returned by read that the synthesis draws on.

subjects.description: Existing public objects this account discusses: select their supplied names, one name per array member. The host binds each name to its object and type. The previous object_type/object_id form is also accepted. This means about, not applies throughout; retain all conditions and exceptions in explanation. Empty means no object attribution supplied.

anyOf.description: An explicitly named subject, without claiming whole-process applicability.

object_id.description: Supplied name of that existing public object.

object_type.description: Type of the existing public object this narrative explicitly discusses.

title.description: The topic's title, in your words.

anyOf.description: Correct only selected text/source fields of one saved or rejected proposal, named by its supplied action_id. Omitted fields keep the exact base. Objects update their named fields; scalars and arrays replace that field. A different value branch must be given completely. Only fields in this edit declaration can change; use a full item for other changes or removal of unknown fields. A stale or unprovable base is refused, never silently rebased. The full candidate still undergoes every original check. Use either the full item or edit, not both.

edit.description: Select one recorded proposal and supply its corrections.

action_id.description: Supplied action name of the exact base proposal.

allOf.description: Selected fields of the verified base proposal.

author_selection_ids.description: Exact TEXT selections to retain as author quotations, copied byte for byte; empty for pure images.

explanation.description: Your source-grounded synthesis of the topic.

selection_ids.description: Selection IDs returned by read that the synthesis draws on.

changes.description: Correct only selected text/source fields of one saved or rejected proposal, named by its supplied action_id. Omitted fields keep the exact base. Objects update their named fields; scalars and arrays replace that field. A different value branch must be given completely. Only fields in this edit declaration can change; use a full item for other changes or removal of unknown fields. A stale or unprovable base is refused, never silently rebased. The full candidate still undergoes every original check. Use either the full item or edit, not both.

repairs.description: Optional. An accepted new version of the same item supersedes its rejected proposal; this does not prove the old scientific claim was saved. To declare a correction/replacement explicitly, give the rejected row's action_id and the corrected item's key in this write, spelled as receipts spell item: collection:index for a listed item, or the envelope's own name.

items.description: Two keys copied from receipts: the rejected row's action_id, the corrected item's item.

action_id.description: Copy the action_id of the rejected row from the receipt that listed it. The host assigns action_ids to receipt rows; items carry none.

item.description: The corrected item's key in this write, spelled as receipts spell item: collection:index for a listed item, or the envelope's own name.

An item sent again with the same route_group_id and repair replaces the saved one; to change the route_group_id or repair of a saved item, quote its item_id. No other id is needed.

changes.description: The changes that stand or fall together, one per fact, written inline.

items.description:
One fact's sparse change. Name the fact in fact_id and write only the properties
being changed. A read returns a complete fact, not a write template: omit unchanged
properties, including empty ones. clear lists optional properties to remove;
withdraw: true with rationale withdraws the whole fact, keeping history. Repair
incoming relations in the same group. Use add_source_ids to add evidence while
retaining earlier evidence. A material is independently addressable.

add_source_ids.description: Add supporting evidence without replacing earlier evidence or resubmitting the content.

after.description: Operation predecessors within its reaction. Preserve or explicitly rebuild order when replacing operations.

category.description: The kind's role: for an OPERATION or NOTE use the task's native fact meanings. For a CONDITION: Prefer one of these keys, written as such: TEMPERATURE: a temperature the reaction is held at or brought to (reflux, -78 °C, rt); several on one operation are its profile in the order written; DURATION: how long the operation or a stage of it runs (2 h, overnight); ATMOSPHERE: the gas the reaction is run under (argon, N2, air, H2 balloon); PRESSURE: the pressure the reaction is run at (4 atm H2, 50 bar); the vacuum of a concentration or distillation is REDUCED_PRESSURE, not this; CONCENTRATION: the concentration of the reaction mixture (0.1 M, c = 0.05 M); the strength of a reagent's solution (2.5 M in hexanes, 1 M in THF) is part of that material's amount phrase, not a condition of its own; SCALE: the amount the operation is run on; on a MATERIAL, how much of it the author used: his whole phrase for the amount, copied as written with every quantity and qualifier in it (26 mg (0.25 mmol, 1 equiv), 1.1 mL (0.55 mmol, 0.5 M in THF), 10 mol %, ten drops); the host reads the amount and the equivalents from it; ADDITION: how or in what order a material is added (dropwise, portionwise, over 30 min, added last); WORKUP: how the reaction is quenched, washed or extracted; purification does not by itself create a separate operation. Its media are QUENCH_WORKUP materials; MICROWAVE: heated by microwave irradiation (MW, μW); PHOTOCHEMICAL: driven by light: a lamp, LED or hv at a wavelength; keeping light out is LIGHT_EXCLUSION; SONICATION: run under ultrasound (sonication, ultrasonic bath); FLOW: run in continuous flow or a flow reactor rather than a flask; SEALED_VESSEL: run in a sealed tube, pressure tube, autoclave or bomb; an ordinary flask is not a condition; DEGASSED: the mixture or solvent was degassed (freeze-pump-thaw, sparged with an inert gas); bubbling a reactive gas through is that gas's ATMOSPHERE; ONE_POT: carried out in the same pot as the preceding operation without isolation (one-pot, telescoped, tandem); STOCK_SOLUTION: how a reagent solution was supplied or handled for use (titrated before use); the strength of a reagent's solution (2.5 M in hexanes, 1 M in THF) is part of that material's amount phrase, not a condition of its own. A separately prepared reagent is one material of the main operation. Its preparation ingredients and preparation conditions belong to another experiment: retain that procedure with its source and explanation, without adding its ingredients or conditions to the main operation. In an experimental reading, ANOTHER_EXPERIMENT keeps the reading separate. Preserve the complete account through the declared narrative entry; if the active declaration offers EXPERIMENT and its operations through skeleton_repairs, use those for an independent experimental graph. A narrative alone does not create that graph.; MONITORING: how completion was judged (monitored by TLC, until consumption of the starting material); STIRRING: a stated stirring or agitation regime (vigorous stirring, rpm); REDUCED_PRESSURE: under vacuum for a concentration, distillation or removal of a volatile (in vacuo, rotary evaporation, reduced pressure); LIGHT_EXCLUSION: kept from light (amber flask, wrapped in foil, in the dark); SOLVENT_RATIO: the proportion of mixed reaction solvents (THF:H2O 4:1, 8:1 THF/1 M NaOH); the solvents themselves are MATERIALs. Chromatography eluents and their ratios belong to QUENCH_WORKUP materials. If none fits, write your own word here and the host keeps the condition with a null key; text is always the author's own words. For a MATERIAL: Choose one of these roles by its meaning: ROUTE_SUBSTRATE: the route compound the operation starts from and transforms, however the author names or numbers it; REAGENT: a substance added to bring the transformation about and consumed by it (a base, an oxidant, a reductant, an organometallic, an acid); CATALYST: a substance that brings the transformation about without being consumed by it (a metal complex, an organocatalyst, an acid or base used catalytically); ADDITIVE: a substance added to the reaction that is neither its reagent, its catalyst nor its solvent (a ligand, a salt, molecular sieves, an initiator, a stabilizer); SOLVENT: the medium the reaction itself runs in; a solvent used only to quench, extract, wash or purify is QUENCH_WORKUP; QUENCH_WORKUP: anything used after the reaction to stop it or to isolate or purify its product: a quench, a wash, an extraction solvent, a drying agent, a chromatography eluent (its ratio kept in its name), silica or celite. For an OUTCOME: Choose one of these kinds by its meaning: ISOLATED_YIELD: the yield of a product the author isolated, with or without its mass (2.65 g (97%), 42 mg (52%), 70% isolated yield); REPORTED_YIELD: a yield the author states without saying how it was determined, as a scheme or the narrative often does (81% over 3 steps, quantitative); ASSAY_YIELD: a yield measured on the unpurified mixture by GC, HPLC or another calibrated assay; NMR_YIELD: a yield measured on the unpurified mixture by NMR against an internal standard; BRSM_YIELD: a yield based on recovered starting material (71% brsm); EE: the product's enantiomeric excess (98% ee); DR: the product's diastereomeric ratio, a single diastereomer included (3:1 dr, >20:1 d.r., single diastereomer); RATIO: any other ratio between products or isomers (E/Z 5:1, a regioisomer ratio, an enantiomeric ratio); RECOVERED_STARTING_MATERIAL: how much starting material was recovered unreacted (15% rsm, 323 mg (37%) of the starting diastereomer); SCALE: how much product a run made where the author states an amount but no yield (1.52 g of 14b); the amount a run is carried out on is the SCALE condition, not this.

clear.description: Explicitly clear optional properties of an existing fact. On a new fact an empty value is simply its default; on an existing fact omission preserves the property and clearing it is said here, never by sending an empty value. Required scientific content and relations cannot be emptied.

extent.description: Condition or measurement scope: whole owners or a substage explained in rationale.

fact_id.description: The fact this change is about: an existing fact by its id as the progress lists it (a read location here instead binds the version you read); a fact created in this write by a name of your choosing, given here and nowhere else. The host binds identity and compares with the version a write naming no view is compared with (view says which).

inputs.description: For a REACTION, the compound facts it consumes: its block boundary.

kind.description: The fact's kind; required for a new fact, omitted for an existing one. Use the native fact meanings in the task instructions.

labels.description: Author-assigned labels only, not names or explanations. For one mixture, give all component labels (9a and 9b); its identity uses the complete label set, not its first member. A single component and the mixture are different identities.

outputs.description: For a REACTION, the compound facts it forms; for an OUTCOME, the products it identifies.

owners.description: Exact subjects: operation belongs to reaction; material to operation; condition to operation OR material; outcome to operations.

rationale.description: Explain the source meaning behind a correction, context role or identity; do not fill missing evidence by inference.

same_as.description: Explicit source-supported identity with another fact. Labels alone do not establish identity. Use clear to remove the relation.

source_ids.description: Keys in the supplied immutable source index supporting the change, never invented citations.

status.description: The fact's evidential status; assign it only to change it.

text.description: Scientific content. For COMPOUND, only its source-supported name or designation; put author labels in labels and explanations in rationale or a sourced NOTE. Names do not establish structure or cross-figure identity. For a MATERIAL: One material name selected from the cited wording. Keep chemically meaningful isotopes, charges and subscripts; a trailing reference marker need not be copied. The host locates the chosen words in the unchanged source; matching is not a chemical identity judgment. For an OUTCOME: The author's words for one reported value, copied as written with the mass and basis written with it ("1.58 g (57% over 2 steps)", "84% brsm", "dr = 3:1"). Two values written together are two phrases: "71% (84% brsm)" is "71%" and "84% brsm". The host reads the number and the basis from these words; do not calculate or restate them. Omission preserves. To remove an optional statement, name it in clear.

withdraw.description: Withdraw this fact with a rationale, keeping history. Fix necessary incoming relations in the same group; no cascade deletion.

reason.description: Why these changes belong together; may be left empty.

repair.description: Existing Fusion changes that must succeed together.

route_group_id.description: The route group supplied under skeleton groups.

two_transformations.description: Record two transformations within an existing operation without splitting it. Identity: operation_id. An item sent again with the same operation_id replaces the saved one; to change the operation_id of a saved item, quote its item_id. No other id is needed.

explanation.description: Explain the two transformations and their source support; this record does not split the public operation.

item_id.description: Host-issued handle returned when this item was first saved; quote it only to change the fields that identify the item (its collection says which), and omit it for a new item.

operation_id.description: Existing operation id that combines two transformations in the source.

withdrawals.description:
Withdraw one saved item, named by its handle or its current returned location.

    Every other item is retained. The handle survives edits; the location names one
    exact version and goes stale when the item is updated.

items.description:
Withdraw one saved item, named by its handle or its current returned location.

Every other item is retained. The handle survives edits; the location names one
exact version and goes stale when the item is updated.

item_id.description: The saved item's host-issued handle, as returned on save.

location.description: The item's current returned location; stale after an update.
